answer.rationale: With the primary contract expiring in 14 days, no auto-renewal, and the line at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, a primary-vendor switch carries unacceptable delivery risk despite memory_c2's attractive cost savings — onboarding was 'quick' historically but never tested under a hard expiry with no slack. Negotiating terms with the incumbent directly serves the 18% cost mandate: memory_c4 shows benchmarking moved the incumbent on price and payment terms, and memory_c6 shows multi-year commitment unlocked volume pricing without narrowing service scope, while memory_c1 confirms continuity keeps integration and deliveries stable. A combined price-benchmark plus multi-year volume ask is the only lever that plausibly approaches the cost target without adding delivery risk. I am verifying memory_c4 (the core negotiation precedent) and memory_c2 (the competing switch option) before committing, since these two memories determine which lever to pull. If verification shows c2's savings vastly exceed what negotiation can reach, a guarded dual-source transition could be reconsidered next cycle — but not under a 14-day deadline.
